note: Hand-derived expected values for ADR-0001 revision 2; see README.md and tools/derive_fixtures.py. runs: [db, n] finite frames, [db, n, 'clipped'], [null, n] non-finite, ['gap', n] missing frames. 50 ms frames; 48 kHz timing (t_audio_ms = frame_index * 50). Not measurements of any real microphone.

cases.description: 100 ms transient (2 candidate frames) is rejected.
cases.derivation: Frames 10-11 are candidates (rel +10). 2 candidate frames < 4: the segment is rejected when the 6th quiet frame ends it. No accepted segments.

cases.description: A frame-aligned 150 ms burst (3 candidate frames) is rejected. Unaligned 150 ms bursts are phase dependent: see vad-phase-sweep.json.
cases.derivation: 3 candidate frames (150 ms) < 4: rejected. (A burst that is not aligned to the 50 ms grid can touch 4 frames: A1-01.)

cases.description: 200 ms (4 frames) is accepted; the onset is the opening frame.
cases.derivation: Candidates are frames 10-13 (4 >= 4, run 4 >= 3). Opening frame 10 = 500 ms. End = end of frame 13 = 14*50 = 700 ms. Duration 200 ms.

cases.description: A gap of 5 non-candidate frames (250 ms) is bridged.
cases.derivation: Candidates 0-3, quiet 4-8 (5 frames, bridged: fewer than 6), candidates 9-10, then quiet. One segment, opening frame 0, last candidate frame 10, 6 candidate frames, longest run 4, end = 11*50 = 550 ms.

cases.description: A gap of 6 non-candidate frames (300 ms) ends the segment.
cases.derivation: Candidates 0-3; the 6th quiet frame (frame 9) ends the first segment at the end of frame 3 = 200 ms. Candidates 10-13 open a second segment [500, 700] ms.

cases.description: The segment ends at its last candidate frame, not after the hangover.
cases.derivation: Candidates are frames 2-5: onset 100 ms, end = 6*50 = 300 ms. The 30 quiet frames add no duration (not 300 + 250 or + 300).

cases.description: Three segments; longest run and sum.
cases.derivation: Seg A frames 0-3 [0,200]; 8 quiet frames (4-11) close it at the 6th. Seg B frames 12-21 [600,1100]; 7 quiet (22-28) close it at the 6th (frame 27). Seg C frames 29-34 [1450,1750]. Spans 200, 500, 300: longest 500, sum 1000.

cases.description: A segment still open when the stream ends is closed at its last candidate frame.
cases.derivation: 10 candidate frames, no offset seen. At finish the segment ends at the end of frame 9 = 500 ms and is marked unterminated (no offset observed).

cases.description: A frame exactly +10.0 dB above the floor opens a segment (A1-03).
cases.derivation: -50 - (-60) = +10.0 >= 10: opens. 4 frames accepted: onset 250 ms, end 450 ms.

cases.description: A frame at +9.9 dB cannot open a segment, so nothing happens at all.
cases.derivation: -50.1 - (-60) = +9.9 < 10: never opens, so no segment is even started (rejected count 0).

cases.description: Once open, frames exactly +6.0 dB continue the segment.
cases.derivation: Frame 5 at +10 opens. Frames 6-8 at -54 are +6.0 >= 6: continuation candidates. 4 candidate frames, run 4: accepted, onset 250 ms, end 450 ms.

cases.description: Once open, a frame at +5.9 dB does not continue the segment.
cases.derivation: Frame 5 opens (+10). Frames 6-8 at +5.9 and the quiet frames are non-candidates; the 6th non-candidate (frame 11) closes the segment with 1 candidate frame: rejected.

cases.description: A steady room at +6 dB for 3 s (the old candidate threshold) never produces a segment.
cases.derivation: Every frame is +6.0 dB: a candidate only once open, but nothing ever reaches +10 to open: no segment, rejected count 0. (Under revision 1 this whole stretch would have been one accepted segment.)

cases.description: Frames at +6 dB before the opening frame are not part of the segment.
cases.derivation: Frames 0-1 at +6 cannot open. Frame 2 at +10 opens: onset 2*50 = 100 ms (not 0). Frames 3-7 at +6 continue: 6 candidate frames, run 6, end = 8*50 = 400 ms.

cases.description: Four isolated clicks 100 ms apart (A1-02).
cases.derivation: Candidates at frames 5, 7, 9, 11: 4 candidate frames in total (the revision 1 rule would accept), but the longest run of consecutive candidates is 1 < 3: rejected.

cases.description: Two pairs of adjacent clicks: 4 candidates, longest run 2.
cases.derivation: Candidates 5-6 and 8-9: 4 candidate frames, longest run 2 < 3: rejected.

cases.description: A run of 3 plus one more candidate (4 in total) is accepted.
cases.derivation: Candidates 5, 6, 7 and 9: 4 candidate frames, longest run 3: accepted. Onset 250 ms, end = 10*50 = 500 ms (the bridged quiet frame 8 is inside the span).

cases.description: A single non-finite frame inside speech is a bridged gap.
cases.derivation: Frames 0-1 candidates, frame 2 non-finite (non-candidate, gap of 1), frames 3-5 candidates. One segment frames 0-5: 5 candidate frames, longest run 3, end = 6*50 = 300 ms.

cases.description: Six consecutive non-finite frames end the segment.
cases.derivation: 6 consecutive non-candidate (non-finite) frames end the first segment at 200 ms; the next 4 candidates are a second segment.

cases.description: A dropout of 2 missing frames inside speech is bridged.
cases.derivation: Candidates at indices 0-3; indices 4-5 missing (non-candidates, gap of 2); candidates at indices 6-7. One segment, 6 candidate frames, longest run 4, end = 8*50 = 400 ms.

cases.description: A dropout of 6 missing frames ends the segment.
cases.derivation: Indices 4-9 are missing: 6 non-candidates end the first segment at 200 ms. Candidates at 10-13 open a second segment.
